title: Gertman and Renban
author: Hempelson Tamsova
rules:
This one innitially was supposed to be a whole Sudoku yet it ended up as a small exercise which could be a tough one nevertheless. During the setting of this puzzle I stumbled across some interesting mechanics regarding the two types and constraints of these lines and how they interact with each other. Every new testing I "discovered" a novel point respectivly proving my previous assumption wrong. So it might be a quick solve for you or you will, like myself, need some time, even though you could just be lucky (as I was a few times aswell) and get the correct solve, just because you forgot to check another possibility.

Find the digit of the black shaded cell (R1C1) and all its positions across the grid.

Normal Sudoku rules apply.

Values of adjacent cells along a thick green line differ by at least 5. Cells along a thin purple line contain a non repeating set of consecutive values in any order (here the 9 is consecutive to 1 aswell, as if the digits 1-9 were arranged like a clock). Any separate line contains exactly one 5, which is the only digit that can have differing values from its natural values.

There are 3 unique values of 5:

G, if it's on a green line.

R, if it's on a purple line.

5, if it's not on a line.

The value of a 5 which appears in a cell sharing two different (coloured) lines counts for both lines independently (meaning it would have two different values simultaneously depending on which of the two lines you focus; i.e. the 5 in such a cell would have the value G for the green line, which is always the same for any green line, and at the same time R for the purple line, which is always the same value for any purple line).

A cell with a small black hexagon in it always contains the same digit.

A grey shaded cell always contains an even digit.

Values of cells in a cage sum to the given total.

solve with SudokuPad

Hint to start

An appropriate start would be in box 3. Think about the number distribution of the lines (in general, instead of focusing too much on individuell numbers along a certain line), the digits and values that must or may not be on a specific type of line and work your way around, use the other given clues mainly if you come across them or if you're stuck. And of course the values of 5 are a, if not the key point.

P.s.
couldn't find a better way of describing the solution code
solutionCode: type in each row number for the target digit from left to right except the given one in column 1, which is the black shaded cell with row number 1. start with column 2 and so on) + the value of 5 appearing on a purple line (9 digits in total, no spaces inbetween)
